abstract: Group II introns are mobile ribozymes that, with their intron-encoded protein (IEP), insert into duplex DNA without a double-strand break, a route to programmed gene insertion so far confined to bacteria. How class IIA complexes recognize and remodel duplex DNA was unknown. We identify group IIA intron/IEP pairs that retrohome efficiently into linear, relaxed duplex DNA, and report cryo-EM structures of one, Voyager-1, at successive stages of insertion. Major- and minor-groove peptides clamp the 5' target and prime melting; intron nucleotides capture one strand; and a peptide linker threads between the re-annealing strands, reading 3' sequence and trapping the HNH nuclease in a nicking-competent position. Guided by these structures, we reprogram protein-encoded specificity, yielding combined RNA and protein-encoded recognition sufficient, by sequence, for single-site targeting in complex plant and animal genomes. Voyager-1 functions when formed in mammalian cells without Mg supplementation, overcoming a long-standing barrier to class IIA introns in eukaryotes.
